items.title: OpenAI shipped GPT-6 to ChatGPT users
items.oneliner: OpenAI put GPT-6 in front of 1.2 billion ChatGPT users, making interface design a model capability now.

items.title: Anthropic cut Haiku pricing hard
items.oneliner: Claude Haiku 5.5 is 75% cheaper than Haiku 4.5, pushing high-volume agent workloads toward commodity pricing.

items.title: OpenAI published its math research dump
items.oneliner: OpenAI released 722 AI-generated math manuscripts across 372 families, but verification remains the real bottleneck.

items.title: Anthropic widened access to cyber models
items.oneliner: Anthropic expanded Claude cyber access after it found real software flaws, signaling offensive capability is already practical.

items.title: Curl is rushing a security release
items.oneliner: Curl will ship fixes for 22 vulnerabilities next week, including one high severity bug worth accelerating the release.

items.title: ShinyHunters pressure is catching up
items.oneliner: ShinyHunters hit a Boeing spin-off before arrests, a reminder that unpatched enterprise software still funds extortion.

items.title: Zeroization can backfire in practice
items.oneliner: Blindly wiping secrets can leave copies in registers or optimized code paths, so your secure erase may be theater.

items.title: Chrome finally shipped JPEG XL
items.oneliner: Chrome 155 adds JPEG XL with 30% to 50% better compression, making modern image pipelines worth revisiting.

items.title: Terminals may get agent status signals
items.oneliner: OSC 7501 proposes a standard way for programs to report blocked, idle, or done states inside terminal workflows.

items.title: Consumer AI spending looks extremely concentrated
items.oneliner: A16z says the top 1% of AI users spend $903 monthly, which should terrify anyone betting on mass subscriptions.
